#2066. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#2063. Birmingham City have a number nine problem to solve when August Priske returns from injury: Opinion

Birmingham City have plenty of reasons to be optimistic about their Championship promotion push, but Jay Stansfield’s recent performances could prove particularly significant. The 23-year-old scored twice against Swansea City, including an 87th-minute winner, to send BCFC top of the table.

He also passed 50 goals for the club before his 24th birthday, underlining his importance since arriving as their record signing. However, it is not just his finishing that makes Stansfield so valuable.

His recent return to the central striker position suggests Chris Davies may have found the best way to get the most out of his €18m-rated forward. However, it may cause an issue with top-scorer August Priske returning from injury.

Across 15 starts and 1,275 Championship minutes this season, Stansfield has registered four goals and one assist, averaging a 7.26 FotMob rating. His 42 shots, 20 efforts on target and 4.88 expected goals demonstrate a consistent appetite for getting into dangerous positions.

Stansfield has frequently operated in attacking midfield during his Birmingham career, but his historical numbers make a compelling argument for keeping him further forward. In 71 appearances as a striker, he has scored 29 goals. By comparison, 46 outings as an attacking midfielder have produced just 12 goals.

That difference is particularly relevant with Priske recently absent. Stansfield has stepped into the central role and responded with three goals across the Millwall and Swansea fixtures, despite accumulating just 1.09 xG in those matches. Against Swansea alone, he registered seven shots and earned a 9.1 FotMob rating.

Crucially, playing centrally does not mean sacrificing his work rate. Stansfield has recorded 39 defensive contributions, including 22 tackles, eight interceptions and 65 recoveries this season.

He is not a conventional target man, winning just 28.6% of his aerial duels, but his mobility, pressing and ability to link play make him a different kind of centre-forward. FotMob’s positional data also highlights why moving him deeper is not necessarily beneficial.

His shot volume and defensive contributions are strengths, whereas his relatively low touches suggest he is not someone who needs to dominate possession to influence matches.

Birmingham invested heavily in Stansfield because of his goalscoring ability, and his record already justifies that faith. With a contract until 2031, there is little reason to reinvent his role.

Priske’s eventual return could give Davies another attacking option, but Stansfield should remain the first-choice striker. The recent evidence suggests Birmingham have a better chance of maximising their record signing when he is leading the line rather than supporting someone else.

#2062. TMW: Milan could replace Estupinan with Atalanta youngster Bernasconi – the details

AC Milan are looking for an upgrade on the left flank, and they have a rising Atalanta star in their sights as per a report.

According to TMW (via PianetaMilan), a target that Milan pursued last summer could become a hot topic again this winter. However, there is competition to overcome, and the pursuit hinges primarily on the future of Pervis Estupiñán.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Milan had a name already circled in red last summer: Lorenzo Bernasconi. The 22-year-old left-back has established himself as a starter with Atalanta, and the Rossoneri have been monitoring his development closely.

The management had already attempted to assess the possibilities of a deal during the last summer transfer window. The player’s possible arrival at Milanello, however, was tied to the sale of Estupiñán which did not happen.

The situation could change in January, when the directors – including the incoming Markus Krösche – will be called upon to reassess the squad composition and the left-back hierarchy. Estupiñán’s performances have so far been less than convincing, and a possible departure cannot be ruled out.

The decision to start Yunus Musah at left-back against Genoa shows Ruben Amorim doesn’t have full faith in the more natural options there, so for this reasons Bernasconi’s name could rise to the top of the list of priorities again.

The problem for Milan is the competition: Roma have also followed the Italian’s development with interest, identifying him as a potential reinforcement for the left flank. The Giallorossi bid €15m for him during the 2026 winter transfer window, but it was turned down.

Newcastle have registered made an interest in the full-back, having reportedly observed him several times through their scouts. With Bernasconi under contract until 2030, it will likely take a figure of €20-25m to convince La Dea to come to the negotiating table.

#2061. Paulo Dybala, rimasto a Roma con uno stipendio molto minore. E ora vuole chiudere lì

Paulo Dybala è al centro della Roma di Gian Piero Gasperini. Come Donyell Malen del resto, oppure Wesley. Giocatori da cui è difficile prescindere, anche se nelle ultime settimane è rimasto fuori per un problema al polpaccio. C'è stato più tempo per Matias Soulé oppure Rodrigo Mora, ottimi nel cercare di sostituirlo, anche se l'argentino è comunque unico, a detta del suo stesso tecnico.

Eppure nel 2024 Dybala rischiava di salutare, in direzione Arabia Saudita. 25 milioni di euro di stipendio sembravano potessero bastare, salvo poi cambiare idea anche perché a Roma ne guadagnava moltissimi: 8 milioni per altre due stagioni più quattro di possibili bonus. Quest'estate invece ha deciso di accettare uno stipendio intorno ai 3,5 milioni di euro.

"Non avrei mai immaginato di fare una carriera del genere qui in Italia. Questo Paese mi ha accolto a braccia aperte, la gente mi ha fatto crescere come uomo e calciatore, ci sono tante emozioni qui, momenti belli e momenti tristi, come poi è la vita di qualsiasi persona. Spero che possa esserci un finale italiano". Dove? "A Roma e con la Roma. Ma è prematuro parlarne ora". Traduzione, dipenderà anche dai contratti che gli verranno proposti, ma fino al prossimo giugno non ci saranno grandi problemi. Oggi Paulo Dybala compie 33 anni.

#2060. Key adjustments and becoming possession-oriented: Tactical analysis of Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan climbed back into the top four in the Serie A table with a much-needed win away against Genoa before the international break.

Milan found themselves two goals up inside 20 minutes when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot and Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos, with both goals coming from the high press.

However, it wouldn’t be the Rossoneri without some late drama, and Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike. Milan did manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

Como’s defeat to Inter means that Ruben Amorim’s men move into the Champions League places, though after the break the pursuit of consistency will continue. Below is the tactical breakdown, from Rohit Rajeev.

Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa’s direct approach immediately put Milan on the back foot, with the hosts threatening to exploit the space behind the defensive line in the opening minute.

They played a long ball into the space behind Koni De Winter, allowing Osmanjic to run in behind and chase the delivery. Although the move appeared to be offside, it served as an early warning of the threat Genoa’s direct approach could pose to Milan’s defence.

Genoa anticipated Milan’s tendency to create numerical overloads in the wide areas and adjusted their defensive structure accordingly.

They used the corresponding centre-back, wing-back and both players from the double pivot to create a 4v3 numerical superiority against Milan’s wide combinations.

This allowed Genoa to outnumber Milan’s attacking players, restrict their progression down the flanks and make it difficult for Amorim’s side to exploit their usual wide overloads.

Milan’s in-possession structure alternated between a 4-1-4-1 and a 3-1-4-2, with the positioning of Musah largely determining which shape the team adopted.

Rabiot occupied the left half-space, while Pulisic preferred to operate closer to Moreira on the right. Meanwhile, Cisse provided the width on the left flank, functioning as Milan’s left winger.

Milan operated with a vertically staggered double pivot, comprising Modric and Rabiot. Modric occupied the deeper position, acting as the midfield screen in front of the back four and providing a link between defence and midfield.

Rabiot, meanwhile, operated higher up the pitch, effectively taking on the role of an attacking midfielder and providing an additional presence between Genoa’s midfield and defensive lines.

The move leading to Cisse’s goal began with Vasquez being tasked with progressing possession from the back. However, Milan managed to create a 3v4 numerical disadvantage for Genoa in the wide areas, forcing Vasquez to recycle possession rather than progress the ball.

Pulisic recognised the opportunity to press and initiated a ball-oriented press, eventually dispossessing Vasquez. He immediately released Rabiot, allowing Milan to exploit the turnover before Genoa could reorganise defensively.

As the possession changed hands, Ramos scanned his surroundings and identified Cisse’s position, recognising the opportunity to attack the space inside the penalty area.

Milan subsequently created a 3v2 numerical advantage inside the box. Cisse initially ran alongside Ramos before checking his run to deceive Marcandalli. This subtle change of movement created separation from his marker and allowed him to attack the space.

Rabiot delivered the cross into the penalty area, where Cisse was perfectly positioned to finish the move and give Milan the lead.

Although Milan adopted a high, man-oriented pressing structure, there were gaps that Genoa could exploit during their build-up. Musah, conscious of the possibility of Genoa creating a 2v1 situation, chose to stay closer to Diawara rather than move out to engage the ball carrier.

This left Ezhibue free to receive possession in the sizeable gap between Musah and Cisse, exposing a weakness in Milan’s pressing structure.

The move leading to Milan’s second goal began with Cisse pressing Traore from behind as the Genoa defender approached the goal line.

Under pressure, Traore attempted a cross-field pass, but Ramos positioned himself intelligently to block the passing lane towards Vasquez.

Rather than attempting to finish the move himself, Ramos showed excellent composure and unselfishly squared the ball into Pulisic’s path, despite Moreira also calling for the pass.

What made the assist particularly impressive was the Portuguese’s execution: he played a no-look pass, deceiving both the goalkeeper and the recovering defender about his intended target. Pulisic capitalised on the opportunity and converted the chance to double Milan’s advantage.

With each passing game Milan are moving into a pure possession-oriented team. In this sequence you can see Pulisic and Rabiot exchanging their positions to confuse their markers

With a 2-0 advantage, Milan shifted towards a more conservative approach, prioritising defensive stability over attacking progression. Amorim reorganised the side into a 5-4-1 defensive structure, adding greater protection to the backline and reducing the spaces available for Genoa to exploit.

However, one of the inherent vulnerabilities of a five-man defensive structure is the space left behind the wing-backs when they are drawn towards the ball.

Genoa looked to exploit this weakness by deliberately dragging Moreira out of his defensive position. As Moreira stepped forward to engage the ball carrier, Gila was forced to jump out of the defensive line to prevent Genoa from creating a 2v1 situation.

This movement consequently opened up space in the right channel, allowing Genoa to exploit an area that would otherwise have been protected by Milan’s compact 5-4-1 defensive block.

Genoa switched from their initial 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-2 formation as they looked to change their attacking approach. El Shaarawy moved into the left midfield position, Vitinha operated on the right, while Baldanzi took up the role of a second striker.

The substitution of Marcandalli also prompted a structural change at the back, with Genoa abandoning their back three in favour of a back four. Ekhator moved into the right-back position, allowing Genoa to maintain a more conventional defensive structure.

For Genoa’s goal, Milan failed to close down Ellertsson, with the defenders seemingly anticipating a cross rather than a shot. Ellertsson recognised the opportunity and noticed that Maignan’s line of sight was obstructed by four Milan defenders.

Taking advantage of the goalkeeper’s limited visibility, he opted to shoot rather than deliver a cross, finding the back of the net.

#2059. Wrexham should revisit Pavel Sulc situation after latest Lyon revelation: Opinion

Wrexham have had a very poor start to the season considering their finish to last year. However, they are a couple of strong January additions away from pushing themselves up towards the Championship play-off picture. One target could be a returning bid for Lyon’s Pavel Sulc.

Phil Parkinson’s side reportedly made the highest offer for the Lyon attacker in the summer of 2026, with their bid understood to be worth approximately £35m. However, Sulc rejected the opportunity, admitting he was not attracted by the prospect of playing in the Championship or moving to a small town in Wales.

That rejection appeared to end Wrexham’s hopes, but Lyon’s financial difficulties have created a potential second opportunity. The French club must sell players during the January window to satisfy financial commitments, and Sulc has emerged as one of their leading candidates for departure.

The 25-year-old has established himself as an exciting attacking talent since joining Lyon from Viktoria Plzen for an initial €7.5m in August 2025. Under contract until June 2029, he can operate as an attacking midfielder, striker or left winger, offering considerable versatility.

His underlying numbers also demonstrate why Wrexham were prepared to spend so heavily. He has 11 goals and three assists in 27 Ligue 1 appearances during his first season at Lyon.

He has also made an encouraging start to 2026/27, registering one goal and three assists in five league appearances, alongside another goal in the Europa League.

His creativity is particularly appealing. Sulc recorded eight chances created in just 417 Ligue 1 minutes this season, while his ability to contribute goals from several attacking positions would address one of Wrexham’s biggest weaknesses.

Parkinson’s side have struggled for attacking consistency, with injuries to Sam Smith, Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead and Callum O’Hare leaving them short of creativity and firepower. Sitting around 15th in the Championship, they need reinforcements if their promotion ambitions are to remain realistic.

There are, however, two significant complications. Sulc underwent surgery on a meniscus injury in October, with his return potentially falling anywhere between January and March. Lyon’s reduced negotiating position could also make a deal more affordable, although his injury represents a genuine availability risk.

His previous comments about the Championship and Wrexham’s location cannot be ignored either. Nevertheless, the club’s continued investment and ambitions could offer a different proposition several months later.

Wrexham should not assume Sulc has changed his mind, but the sporting circumstances and Lyon’s financial position have shifted. Given their need for attacking quality, reopening the conversation would certainly be worthwhile.

#2057. GdS: ‘Ahead of the curve’ – Amorim’s positive start compared to predecessors

Ruben Amorim might not have unanimously won everyone over yet, but AC Milan are off to their best Serie A start in four years.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write this morning that Milan under Amorim have started better than under Massimiliano Allegri in 2025-26, Paulo Fonseca in 2024-25 and even Stefano Pioli’s final season in 2023-24.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The best start belongs to the coach who delivered the Scudetto though, with 31 points in the first eleven rounds of the 2021-22 season, which ended with the most recent Italian league title added to the trophy cabinet.

Amorim has also hit the ground running, with an average that, in previous seasons, would have placed him even higher. A year ago, with 24 points at this same stage of the tournament, Milan would have been the league leaders.

The numbers don’t lie: 24 out of a possible 33 points – garnered through seven wins, three draws, and only one Serie A defeat – amount to 2.18 points per match. By comparison, Allegri had reached 22 points, Fonseca 17 and Pioli also had 22 in his final year.

The coach behind the 2021-22 Scudetto also started with great momentum in the previous season (26 points in 2022-23) and in the 2020-21 campaign (27 points).

These figures were double the 13 points from the 2019–20 season, a campaign that began with Marco Giampaolo at the helm, only for him to be replaced mid-season by Pioli. While still seeking to find that same rhythm in Europe, Milan have been surging in the league.

They got off to a blistering start with wins away at Torino and in their San Siro debut against Venezia, followed by a draw at Juventus – a match in which they were pegged back just minutes from the end -and another stalemate away to Lazio.

After falling two goals behind, Milan fought back against the team currently leading the league. Given Lazio’s subsequent form, that result takes on added significance. Next came a victory over Lecce, followed by a lacklustre draw in Reggio Emilia against Sassuolo.

From that point on, the turning point arrived: four wins in the next five matches, including away victories against Udinese and Genoa away from home, as well as the derby. The only stumble during this stretch was against Bologna.

Sensing that the squad was under significant stress, Amorim has granted a week off, with training set to resume next Monday. For those without other commitments such as international duty, this provides a chance to truly switch off.

Many players have headed away, while those who remained are either following strict injury recovery programs or simply taking a break. This pause is longer than usual: the typical break in professional leagues is generally shorter.

This isn’t the only unusual aspect: the return to training ahead of the match against Frosinone the following week will also take place only after the players returning from international duty have been given ample time to rest.

There are precedents for this, though. For instance, the team was given a Tuesday off just two days before their European away match against Bournemouth. They returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they departed for England. The result was a 3-0 loss and a dark night.

There is certainly enough evidence now to speak of new methods introduced by Amorim and his staff. On the pitch, Rúben has brought in new ideas: training sessions are never overly gruelling, and the data from GPS trackers and distance-monitoring tools is never pushed to ‘excessive’ levels.

“We train by playing,” the Portuguese coach has often explained, implying that matches themselves offer the best opportunities to test tactical schemes and movements. This is especially the case when playing every three days, with such little time between games.

While this approach may have initially raised some eyebrows among the players and was even speculated to be a cause for the cluster of injuries the Rossoneri experienced, such concerns were dispelled once the coach provided further clarification.

In the meantime, no one is taking a break fully. Even while away, every player has been assigned specific training programs to follow, ensuring they return in peak condition to keep the good league form going.

#2056. Sheffield Wednesday injury update on Louie Barry pre-Plymouth Argyle clash

Sheffield Wednesday have been without the winger since early September due to an ankle injury. SWFC are back in League One action this weekend with a home clash against Plymouth Argyle at Hillsborough.

Barry, 23, was snapped up by the Owls over the summer on a permanent basis from Aston Villa and he penned a four-year deal with the South Yorkshire outfit until June 2030, with the option of a further 12 months on top of that. He has since made six appearances in all competitions this season and has chipped in with three goals and one assist.

In this latest update regarding his condition, his head coach Challinor has said, as per the official club website: “We hope to see him back certainly within the coming weeks. Maybe Saturday; we’ll see what the next few days look like.”

Sheffield Wednesday are positioned in 9th place in the table after their first 13 fixtures and they are two points off the play-offs behind Reading in 6th. They have drawn their last two league outings on the spin against Cambridge United and Blackpool.

Sheffield Wednesday will be looking forward to having Barry back. SWFC’s form hasn’t been great over recent times.

The Owls have won only one of their last eight matches in all competitions. Challinor knows Barry well from their time at Stockport County together and has managed to get the best out of him in the past.

Barry was signed by his current club in the last transfer window to bolster their attacking department. When fit, he will give them more competition and depth to pick from at the top end of the pitch.

The ex-England youth international was on the books of Aston Villa from 2020 to 2026. He played once for their first-team and was loaned out to Ipswich Town, Swindon Town, MK Dons, Salford City, Hull City and Sheffield United, as well as Stockport County, to get some experience under his belt and to boost his development.

Barry is a proven performer at third tier level and will inject some serious quality into Sheffield Wednesday’s starting XI. SWFC fans will be excited to see him back in action for them.

Challinor will be eager to get a win over Plymouth Argyle on Saturday afternoon. He has lost his first two outings against Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley in the FA Cup and EFL Trophy respectively.

The new Owls’ manager will get the chance to put his own stamp on his newly inherited squad with some signings in January. He will also have the opportunity to offload some players if needed.

#2055. Guerra per la Federcalcio: cronaca semiseria di una commedia all’italiana

Quella che segue è una ricostruzione accurata eppure di totale fantasia degli ultimi sette mesi del calcio italiano, nel corso dei quali abbiamo: fallito la qualificazione al terzo mondiale consecutivo, cambiato due presidenti, nominato un commissario straordinario, scoperto l’obbligo del tesseramento, discusso della possibilità di revocare una firma, cambiato cavallo almeno due volte. Ogni riferimento a fatti e persone realmente esistenti è frutto della fantasia dell’autore, ma puramente voluto.

“Buonasera dottor Malagò, le va di fare il presidente della Federcalcio?”.

“Ma scusate, tra qualche giorno giochiamo con la Bosnia… Aspettate almeno quella, povero Gravina”.

“Ma no, ma no. Bisogna essere pronti a qualsiasi evenienza: lei è il più vincente dirigente sportivo italiano, conosciuto all’estero, con Milano Cortina ha fatto ancora una volta il pieno di ori. Sì, per carità, l’ultima volta che abbiamo avuto a che fare con lei non ci siamo stati tanto simpatici, ma acqua sotto i ponti. Le va di fare il presidente della Federcalcio?”.

“Guardate, mi sembra prematuro. Aspettiamo almeno la Bosnia”.

Interno giorno, primavera… qualche tempo dopo.

“Buongiorno dottor Malagò, le va di fare il presidente della Federcalcio?”

“Abbiate pazienza, con la Bosnia ci giochiamo domani, magari andiamo ai Mondiali e c’è Gravina. Aspettate”.

“Mi scusi, eh. Ma questi non sono affari suoi: vuole fare il presidente della Federcalcio sì o no?”.

“Insomma… non ci avevo pensato. Ma lei mi dice di rappresentare la Serie A: io non me la ricordo così unita, quando ho fatto il commissario di Lega eravate pronti a linciarmi per l’elezione di Micciché. Sicuri che siate tutti, tutti convinti?”.

“Ma sì, ma sì. Ma questo poi si sistema, non si preoccupi. Lei vuole fare il presidente della Federcalcio?”.

Esterno stadio, primavera… il giorno dopo.

“Allora, dottor Malagò, è tutto pronto. Lei farà il presidente della Federcalcio. Siamo 18 società, forse 19 su 20, manca solo Lotito ma lei, insomma, lo conosce. E poi siete romani, sbrigatevela voi. In più abbiamo a bordo anche calciatori e allenatori”.

“Perfetto! Non vedo l’ora. Ma qual è il programma?”.

“Ma sì, ma poi ci si pensa. Intanto farà il presidente della Federcalcio. Ah, punto primo: cambiare il segretario generale. Ci tengono soprattutto calciatori e allenatori, valgono il 30%”.

“Ok, non mi pare una priorità. Ma sì, vi prometto che lo farò. Le altre componenti che ne pensano?”.

“Ma chi? Abbiamo il 46,8% dei voti. Lei non riesce a rimediare qualche altro voto in giro per l’Italia? È Malagò… E poi, mi scusi, ma cosa vuole che dicano? Lei è Malagò”.

“Per carità, ha ragione. Il programma quando lo stiliamo? Avete qualche idea per il commissario tecnico?”.

“Ma sì, sì, al programma poi ci pensiamo. Ma ci sembra che ci possa essere un solo nome possibile. Non ci si può sbagliare. E poi ha già fatto il ct”.

“Buongiorno, presidente Malagò. Con Maldini e Leonardo ci ha provato, ma pazienza…”.

“Sì, ma poi anche loro, proporre Pirlo. Per fortuna è saltato fuori lo sponsor russo”.

“Vabbè. Ora puntiamo sul nome giusto che avevamo detto?".

"Ah, strano, ho parlato prima con Antonio e mi ha detto che non vi eravate ancora sentiti".

"Antonio? E chi è? No, no: io ho chiamato l'unico nome possibile. Roberto Mancini sarà il ct".

“Ma è rimasto sorpreso? E non le ho ancora detto il capodelegazione. Un grandissimo nome dello sport italiano, incredibile”.

“Presidente, scusi, ma il segretario generale? Si ricorda che avevamo un accordo?”.

“Certo, ma fatemi lavorare. Abbiamo appena scelto insieme il ct, ci sono tante cose da fare”.

“Ma era il primo punto del nostro programma”.

“E allora ci risentiamo. Non vi preoccupate, l'ho promesso”.

“Presidente Malagò, abbiamo un problema”.

“Si ricorda quando a giugno è stato eletto presidente della Federcalcio?”.

“Una tessera? Ma ho organizzato le Olimpiadi, sono stato presidente del Coni dodici anni. Che tessera?”.

“Quella della Figc, presidente. C'è stato un ricorso”.

“Strano, i miei dicono che ho ragione io”.

“E quindi bisogna commissariare la Federcalcio”.

“Quindi non posso fare il presidente, però posso fare il commissario e ricandidarmi per fare il presidente?”.

“Commissario Malagò, abbiamo un problema”.

“Come dieci? E calciatori e allenatori?”.

“Ma non erano quelli che volevano cambiare il segretario generale?”.

“Pronto, senatore Galliani? Le andrebbe di fare il presidente della Federcalcio?”.

“Sì, ma ci sono state delle incomprensioni”.

“Poi ci pensiamo. Intanto abbiamo il 30% dei voti”.

“Non si preoccupi, tanto lì non sono mai tutti d'accordo”.

“Va bene. Ma fatemi controllare una cosa: mi sono tesserato, vero?”.

“Commissario Malagò, ottime notizie. Abbiamo undici firme”.

“Il Genoa ha firmato anche per Galliani”.

“No, ha cambiato idea. Però Galliani dice che la prima firma non si può revocare”.

“Sentite, nominiamo una commissione per questo. Magari con un generale”.

“Commissario Malagò, abbiamo un problema”.

“No, questa volta c'è un ricorso. Di Galliani”.

“Contesta la commissione che lei ha nominato”.

“Ma se l'ho nominata proprio per essere sicuro che sia tutto regolare!”.

“Dice che non può essere lei, che è candidato, a nominare chi verifica le candidature”.

“Ma no: diciamo che la commissione mica decide. Aiuta soltanto il segretario generale”.

“Un ottimo avvocato, socio del Circolo Aniene. Però fa parte anche del Collegio di Garanzia del Coni”.

“No, eravamo impegnati con le firme e i ricorsi. Che ha fatto?”.

“Ha battuto la Francia. Abbiamo una bella squadra”.

“Ah, meraviglioso. E chi è il commissario tecnico?”.

“Ma che c'entra il segretario generale?”.

“Scusate, ormai è diventata un'abitudine”.

#2054. Moretto: Milan’s plan for rising star Cisse clear as Brighton see approach rejected

Alphadjo Cisse is attracting interest after his red-hot start to the season, and AC Milan are already rejecting advances.

Cisse is undoubtedly the story of the season for Milan so far. Having officially signed from Hellas Verona in January, he was allowed to remain on loan with Catanzaro in Serie B before suffering a serious injury that needed surgery. After a few months out, a loan was even evaluated.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, Ruben Amorim saw something in the 20-year-old and made him a big part of his plans. His faith has been rewarded, given that Cisse has eight goals in 12 appearances in all competitions so far this season, with the latest coming against Genoa on Sunday.

These numbers have naturally attracted the interest of several European clubs, but there is also talk of a renewal. Matteo Moretto explained things in a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan are rejecting verbal offers from several clubs. Milan are already saying no to several clubs for Cisse. There are several Premier League clubs, and I’ll name one, Brighton,” the journalist began.

“Milan have already said no and wants to renew his contract. And they will renew his contract, which currently expires in 2030. There will be a salary adjustment. Born in 2006, nine games and five goals [in Serie A]. Incredible talent, just called up by Mancini.

“I also want to give credit to the old Rossoneri management, because whoever signed him – the Furlani-Moncada duo – snatched him from PSV, who had practically sealed the deal. When the player saw Milan appear, he had no doubts and turned down PSV.

“Even the sporting project, sending him on loan to Catanzaro, was key for the player. Because the path was the right one, and today we can see the results. Milan paid €8m, having tried to sign him in previous years from Verona Primavera. Congratulations to Milan and to all the management linked to Cisse.”
