#2042. Expected Points and clinical shooting: Stats highlight worries about sustainability of Milan’s Serie A form

AC Milan have collected more points than they deserved so far in the 2026-27 Serie A season, according to statistical data.

As MilanPress write, the Expected Points ranking makes for worrying reading. The metric compares the points actually earned by Serie A teams with those expected based on performances and chances created and conceded in the first 11 rounds of the league season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have earned 24 points compared to approximately 17 expected, meaning they are ‘over-performing’ by seven points. Milan are currently fourth in the table behind Lazio, Inter and Roma, but they should be a few places lower.

Inter are second with 28 actual points, but should have collected around 26, while Juventus are on 18 points earned versus the expected 21. Napoli also obtained less than the data indicated they should have, with 15 actual points compared to the approximately 19 expected.

The numbers, therefore, reveal a Milan that is particularly effective in turning its performances into tangible results. This is a positive aspect in terms of the league table, but also food for thought. Is it sustainable moving forwards?

Another interesting statistic has come from Kickest, which perhaps highlights why Ruben Amorim’s side have been able to out-perform what the data suggests.

They reveal that there are 113 players with at least 10 shots in Serie A so far in 2026-27. The top four with the best conversion rates have something in common: they play for the Diavolo.

➤ Rabiot — 41.7% (5 goals) ➤ Moreira — 40.0% (4) ➤ Cisse — 38.5% (5) ➤ Pulisic — 36.4% (4) ➤ De Bruyne — 30.0% (3)

It is reminiscent of something we published in January, when the shooting numbers under Massimiliano Allegri were similarly remarkable. As we know, a late-season collapse ended up coming.

Then there was the revelation from Sky after the Genoa game, as they looked at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. So, Milan must get much better at generating and sustaining pressure, or the results might start to regress.

#2041. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

“I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

“We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”

Why they didn’t follow the plan that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

“We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

On top of that problem, they were vulnerable to Newcastle’s pace and direct play early on although that threat abated as the half progressed. Jaissle will be delighted with the commitment and application of his players, but Osula may have to come off with a knock.

Isak hooks a pass towards Frimpong straight out of play, causing much mirth among the home fans.

Foul given against Wissa on Gravenberch, and the Newcastle forward needs to be careful on a yellow. I’m not sure there was any contact at all. Wissa drags a shot across the face of Liverpool’s goal and wide.

Gravenberch with a speculative shot which is blocked, before Dedic blasts the ball off Gakpo to win a goal kick. Dan Burn is watching on from the stands, Newcastle’s new club captain who is absent because of a rolled ankle. Also up there in the gods is England manager Thomas Tuchel.

Much better cross from Frimpong, but Dedic clears at the back post for a Liverpool corner. Danger as Gakpo flicks the ball on at the neat post, and the ball bounces off Botman and behind for another corner. Gravenberch tries a cute reverse pass towards Isak, but it deflects through to Hornicek. Isak has been ever so quiet.

William Osula is hobbling up top for Newcastle, which is a worry because has been a menace so far. The same can be said of Yoane Wissa who is having a stormer as a second striker, dropping into midfield at times.

Stuart Atwell being a little card happy, now Lewis Miley is shown a yellow for a foul on Gravenberch. Just looked a regulation midfield foul, not sure a booking was necessary.

Osula took the free-kick, straight into the wall, but his follow up effort deflects off Szoboszlai and behind for a corner. Excellent delivery from Lewis Hall, cleared by Van Dijk.

Wirtz and Isak do well down the left to start a Liverpool counter with runners forward, but Frimpong’s delivery from the right is atrocious.

Liverpool starting to monopolise possession, without a crafty final pass. Kerkez has been booked for holding Elanga, who is giving him a going over on Newcastle’s right flank.

Then Barnes rolls inside Frimpong and drives inside, and the Liverpool right-back is booked for a challenge from behind. May well have been a harsh call, both plays were grasping for a piece of shirt.

Both of Liverpool’s full-backs on yellows now.

Wissa booked for a mistimed challenge, and Liverpool have a free-kick 30 yards out. Szoboszlai is thinking about a shot... but he blasts his shot straight into the wall.

Osula then does very well to make it stick and drag Newcastle up the pitch but the move fizzles out.

It’s an experience in itself watching Andoni Iraola on the sideline. He’s going to have clocked up 10,000 steps for sure by the final whistle and his increasing animation is indicative of Liverpool’s anaemic start. You would expect Liverpool to score at some point but this is a team that has lots of questions to answer.

Isak down on the turf after a strong challenge by Lewis Hall, no foul given much to the delight of the Newcastle fans.

Then the home team cut through Liverpool again, Wissa with a glorious outside of the foot pass behind Jacquet for the run of Osula, but the Liverpool defender just about got a toe to the ball as the striker closed in on Alisson. Great challenge in the end from the wrong side.

Nice counter-movement between Elanga and Dedic the right-back. Elanga faked to drop inside, taking Kerkez and Gakpo with him, and Miley’s switch found Dedic on the outside. Cross is blocked, and Newcastle have a corner. Cleared, and then a poor Szoboszlai pass is blocked when there was a chance to release Wirtz on the counter.

It feels like all the 50:50s are dropping Newcastle’s way at the moment. It has been a very energetic start, the question is whether that is sustainable across the game so early in the season. The tempo will surely drop at some point.

Peter Beardsley, Tino Asprilla and Shaka Hislop among Keegan’s former players watching on.

Hornicek with his first big save of the game, tipping Wirtz’s shot around the post. Newcastle failed to deal with a Kerkez cross and the ball dropped to the German for a snap shot. Newcastle defend the corner.

“There’s only one greedy b-----d,” is the chant from the Newcastle fans (aimed at Isak, for the uninitiated).

Wissa goes down looking for a foul but nothing doing, but there are cheers from the home fans as Isak is beaten to a header and then Sean Steur turns away from pressure well in midfield. There is more bite about the home team in the challenges than Liverpool, Jaissle will be delighted with this.

Echoes of last season with Liverpool’s defence looking suspect against direct play, Alisson with an unconvincing intervention outside his penalty area after the ball held up. He is fortunate that Wissa did not connect with the volley when there was a chance to lob the goalkeeper.

What a difference a year makes. Anthony Elanga was played in on goal against Aston Villa on his Premier League debut for Newcastle United 12 months ago. He looked nervous and hit a tame effort too close to the goalkeeper.

It is fair to say that was a sign of things to come for the winger who endured a miserable first season on Tyneside following a high-profile £55m move from Nottingham Forest. He looked drained of confidence and lacked the composure and technical ability to succeed in black and white stripes.

Fast forward 12 months and he has just taken a very similar chance against Liverpool. The speed of Will Osula sent the visiting defence into retreat, and his pace and excellent first touch set up the chance, which he finished clinically.

That was the player Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer. It was the player Newcastle supporters thought was going to offer a major upgrade in the right wing position.

If Elanga has a better season this time around it will be a huge boost to new manager Matthias Jaissle.

Elanga vs Kerkez is a match-up which looks advantageous for Newcastle, the Liverpool left-back is at full tilt to get back and by a foul after a lofted Wissa pass over his head towards the rapid Sweden winger.

This is a very open game already, and Liverpool are back on the front foot. Szoboszlai whips in a free-kick which appears to glance of Van Dijk’s head, but the referee awards a corner. Hall clears, but Newcastle do not clear their lines and Gakpo’s shot is blocked by Thiaw.

Liverpool caught out on the break, but it is a really well-executed goal from Newcastle’s perspective. Gravenberch should have let fly at the other end, but after the move broke down Osula was able to receive in space and turn to face Van Dijk and Jacquet. He waited for the support of Elanga to arrive, and he burned down the outside of Kerkez. Well-weighted pass put him through, and the finish across Alisson was ideal.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

Lewis Hall wins a challenge at the edge of the box which receives a roar of approval from the crowd, but Liverpool quickly settle into a long spell of possession, with Gravenberch turning away from pressure, but neglecting to shoot.

This already has the feel of a very helter-skelter game. Newcastle won a free-kick inside 20 seconds, clipped into the penalty area but it was claimed by Alisson. Then a Liverpool attack swept from one end to the other with Wirtz’s shot blocked at the edge of the box. This should be tasty.

That roar turns to vociferous boos as Alexander Isak takes the kick-off.

They would have still been clapping until tomorrow if the whistle hadn’t been blown by referee Stuart Attwell to start the game but the flip from adulation for Kevin Keegan to absolute vitriol towards Alexander Isak was incredible. 50,000 in black and white are singing a song aimed at him. The only two words we can get away with printing are “ole, ole!” - use your imagination for what might have preceded it!

A period of applause for Kevin Keegan at St James' Park 👏❤️ pic.twitter.com/AsSGOkpVPN

There is a minute’s applause for Keegan, which ends with a defending roar.

Liverpool have just taken to the field for their warm up, predictably to a back drop of pantomime booing. But there is a nice touch from the club, as each member of Andoni Iraola’s squad is wearing a jersey with “Keegan 7” on the back. It’s going to be a day of heavy emotion.

Alan Shearer was one of those fans holding up a white card:

The Keegan quote on the Newcastle banner is: “I want people to dream about their football club. They should, we should all be dreamers at heart. Some people are the opposite and say ‘we can’t do that’, but when you ask them why, they can’t give a reason. Well, I say, ‘Why not?’”

Banners are being unfurled in the Gallowgate End. Alan Shearer and Stuart Pearce are in the stands, and Les Ferdinand is pitchside speaking on Sky.

As you know it’s a transition phase and a huge challenge. There will be some activity in the transfer market new week, hopefully, but we go for it, we are as ready as we can be. That’s something we want to show the fans, we want to go all in.

As soon as I saw him on the pitch, I was falling in love. He is a great guy with great potential.

I’m not worried. As a manager, a player or a squad, if it is against you you want to play this kind of games.

Difficult call, Jeremy has very good skills with the ball, without the ball they will be very demanding today, playing against Wissa and Osula.

Alexander Isak is going to be in for the sort of hostile afternoon unseen in English football for years.

Not since Michael Owen has a player left Newcastle and been so universally despised. Owen was accused of ducking out of a relegation battle to ensure he secured a lucrative free transfer move after an injury-ravaged spell in the North East.

If anything, Isak was even worse, He went on strike, refusing to play for the club again, despite having three years left on his contract, in order to force a move to Liverpool. It felt like the ultimate betrayal and crossed a line with Geordies. They will love you and worship players as good as Isak, but if you behave like the Sweden international did you become the ultimate villain.

Isak was a superb player in black and white stripes, arguably their best since the takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in 2021. He was top goalscorer two years running and was the focal point of Eddie Hower’s attack as they qualified for the Champions League twice and won the Carabao Cup.

He could have been a Geordie legend, but he left in such an ugly and acrimonious fashion. Isak forced Newcastle to buckle from their not for sale stance, rejecting a pay rise and a new contract, insisting he would never play for the club again even if they refused to sell him, that he will be tarnished forever.

It is sad in many ways and shows the ugly side of the game. I’m told he does regret the manner of his exit, especially his falling out with Howe. They have not spoken since. It has weighed heavily on him since his move to Anfield.

Looks like Rio Ngumoha will play on the right flank with Cody Gakpo left, Wirtz in the No 10 role behind Isak.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Frimpong, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak

The Reds to take on Newcastle in our season opener ✊ #NEWLIV

Barnes, Wissa, Osula and Elanga start in what could be a front four. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur, just 20 and 18 respectively, will need to get through an immense amount of work in midfield.

Newcastle United XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Miley, Steur; Elanga, Wissa, Barnes; Osula

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Bobby Moncur are the representatives of both clubs with wreaths, and Shola Ameobi is behind Dalglish. Ian Rush is also in attendance, who spent one season on Tyneside in the twilight of his career when Dalglish was the manager.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. That will surely sting Liverpool fans more than most, given the city’s strong sense of regional identity. You can read more on the subject in this article by Dominic King. Trent on loan in January, anyone?

He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

These are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.Full team news on the way shortly.

#2040. All 24 EFL Championship clubs ranked by how successful they've been in the last 25 years

There has been a lot of success to go around the 24 teams currently competing in the Championship over the last 25 years.

What defines success to a club is different for everyone, and the wider context of a team’s history can make a National League title more significant than coming second in a higher division.

From Birmingham City to Wrexham, all of the teams in the second division this year have achieved a piece of history for their club.

But not all success is created equal, from winning the EFL and FA Cups, to simply achieving promotion through the play-offs.

Here we rank the 24 Championship sides based on how successful they’ve been since 2001/02…

Blackburn Rovers won the Premier League title in 1995, but that was over 30 years ago now, and they have yet to come close to that kind of success since.

In just the last 25 years, the Lancashire outfit have a second place in League One in 2018 as their greatest success, with their highest league finish being sixth in the Premier League in 2003 and 2006.

Preston North End were one of the most successful clubs in the very early days of organised football in the UK.

However, the Lilywhites have not many major achievements to celebrate over the last 25 years, with their greatest success in this period being their 2015 play-off victory in League One.

Stoke City came close to achieving the greatest success in their history in 2011 when they lost the FA Cup final to Manchester City.

Instead, the Potters have had to settle for play-off victory as their greatest moment of success in the last 25 years, earning promotion to the second tier in 2002.

Millwall came close to automatic promotion to the Premier League in 2025, but had to settle for the play-offs, where they lost to Hull City in the semi-finals.

But they have achieved play-off success in the last 25 years, twice winning the competition at a League One level (2010 & 2017).

Charlton Athletic were competing in the Premier League 25 years ago, and have fallen to League One in the time since.

But their 2012 title victory in the third tier remains an impressive achievement, and they have also won the play-offs at that level twice in this period (2019 & 2025).

Watford won the Championship play-offs in 2006 under Aidy Boothroyd to earn their place in the Premier League.

But their closest brush with real success came in the 2019 FA Cup final, where they lost to Manchester City in a 6-0 defeat.

Southampton have brushed up against big success in the last 25 years, reaching both an FA Cup and EFL Cup final in this period, as well as coming second in the Championship in 2011.

But their greatest achievement since 2001 was their 2024 play-off final victory, which earned Russell Martin’s side a place in the Premier League.

Bolton Wanderers’ decline from Premier League side to League Two outfit occurred within the last 25 years, which meant a lot of difficult campaigns for supporters.

FLW have looked at the individuals who are currently taking home the second tier's biggest wages

The most recent season saw Steven Schumacher’s side win the League One play-offs, which may be their greatest achievement of this entire period, although the 2023 EFL Trophy victory is also a moment fans will remember fondly for years to come.

Wrexham spent several seasons competing at a non-league level during this 25-year period, but they’ve enjoyed a remarkable rise under their Hollywood ownership in the few campaigns.

The Red Dragons’ greatest success in this timeframe was their National League title victory in 2023, which they won with a staggering 111 points, before going on to earn two more automatic promotions in the following two years.

Derby County’s greatest successes all came in the post-World War years, with the high watermark being two league titles in the 1970s.

But over the last 25 years, the Rams’ biggest achievement was their 2007 play-off final victory under Billy Davies, which earned them a place in the Premier League.

#2039. GdS: A start vs. France at San Siro – Cisse’s rapid ascent continues with Mancini’s faith

Alphadjo Cisse continues to go from strength to strength, and his biggest moment yet might be coming during the break.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, beyond the confidence with which he plays and speaks, what’s truly striking is Cisse’s composure in front of goal at just 20 years of age, experiencing his first proper season in the top flight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His goal in Genoa seemed easy because he made it so, but it wasn’t. Adrien Rabiot’s pass was quite slow, the distance to the goal wasn’t that close, Genoa were exposed after losing the ball but Bijlow wasn’t in a particularly bad position, and beating him required precision.

Other strikers in those circumstances may have opted for a powerful finish. Not Cisse. He looked for the corner and found it with a lovely precise strike, one which revealed everything about the groove he has found himself in.

It was goal number five in the league for Alphadjo Cisse, making him Milan’s joint-top scorer alongside Rabiot. That extends to eight across all competitions, which puts the young Italian alone on the pedastal.

Two stats in particular stand out. The first: with his fifth goal in his ninth league appearance at 20 years and 17 days, he became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Pato (18 years and 181 days).

Second: he is one of only three players born in 2006 or later in the five major European leagues in 2026-27 to have scored at least eight goals in all competitions, along with Yamal (13) and Brunner (8).

Oh, and there’s another pretty good one: Shevchenko also scored eight goals in his first 13 games of the season with the Diavolo (although he achieved this in fewer minutes). The reward could well be a renewal, to fend off Premier League interest too.

🇮🇹 “The San Siro boys. Esposito plus Cissé: Mancini looks to a Milanese Italy.”

🤔 “Esposito is a lock at centre-forward, the debutant Alphadjo could join him in the attacking trio against France. Could Zaniolo be there too?” pic.twitter.com/zCkNmyqISY

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 10, 2026

Now, a change in dressing room awaits over the break. Roberto Mancini called him up to the senior national team for the first time, and according to La Gazzetta, the talent could start immediately.

He’s currently competing for a spot on the left in the 4-3-3 formation with Cambiaghi and Sebastiano Esposito. The Rossoneri guarantees more presence in the penalty area and quality in finishing, while Cambiaghi provides more coverage.

We’ll see if Mancini ultimately chooses to use him from the start, but what’s certain is that the former Verona man will be ready no matter what, and for a game at San Siro against France no less.

#2038. Supercomputer predicts full 2027/28 EFL Championship table if Man Utd & Man City are in it

There is a very real possibility, as things stand, that Manchester United and Manchester City could be playing Championship football next season, as Football League World takes a closer look at what the division could look like next year with those two involved.

Heading into the international break, Manchester United occupy one of the bottom three places, with only Crystal Palace and Sunderland beneath the Red Devils as things stand, with just one win in their opening ten Premier League games.

Michael Carrick has been dismissed from his post at Old Trafford, as it appears as though former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur head coach Mauricio Pochettino will leave his post as the USMNT boss to head to the English North West to save the global giants.

Manchester City, meanwhile, sit 3rd in the Premier League right now beneath Brighton & Hove Albion and Arsenal. With seemingly no chance of relegation based on that, the Citizens await the verdict on the outcome after being found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them relating to financial wrongdoing and non-cooperation.

A heavy punishment is almost certainly heading their way, with expulsion or a heavy points deduction being bandied about, as Football League World takes a look at what the 2027/28 EFL Championship table would look like, according to AI, if both Manchester clubs suffered the drop.

AI has predicted Birmingham City, Middlesbrough, and Stoke City to be promoted to the Premier League, whilst Burnley, Derby County, and Preston North End head to League One.

AI says: Struggle with the step up in quality and lack the squad depth to compete consistently.

Coming in at 24th is Lincoln City, as whilst the Imps manage to survive their first campaign in the Championship, AI believes they do not have what it takes to sustain themselves in the second tier for another year.

The financial disparity between Lincoln and the rest of the Championship right now is clear to see, and despite the financial influx of another year in the second tier, AI backs the side from Sincil Bank to be unable to build upon that historic finish and head back down to League One.

AI says: A difficult season, with an inconsistent attack and too many dropped points.

Charlton Athletic were top of the Championship table after three games, with victories over Derby County, Preston North End, and West Ham United to begin the season.

However, just one win in their following 12 has seen the Addicks slip down the table under Nathan Jones, who, for the first time in his time at The Valley, faces increased pressure to turn results around.

AI backs the Welshman to guide them to safety this year, but next year, it believes they won't be so fortunate.

AI says: Enjoy a few good moments after promotion but find the Championship a step too far.

Oxford United spent two years in the Championship between 2024 and 2026, suffering the drop back into League One at the end of last season alongside Leicester City and Sheffield Wednesday.

Out of those three clubs, the U's have adapted best to the trials and tribulations of the third tier, having kept the core members of their squad, such as Cameron Brannagan, Michel Helik, and Mark Harris.

AI believes they will be promoted this year, but after just one year back in the second tier, they will take the final relegation place.

AI says: Competitive in spells but lack the consistency needed to challenge higher up the table.

Bolton Wanderers, following promotion back to the Championship for the first time since 2019 last season, have not looked out of place upon their return to the division, with Steven Schumacher's side playing some wonderful stuff.

AI thinks they will have enough to avoid the drop this year, but not quite enough to build upon that success, and though, by its prediction, Bolton will spend a third year in the Championship, it will be only just, finishing narrowly above the drop zone, and cutting it too close for comfort.

AI says: A fairly difficult campaign, with a mid-table squad that struggles against stronger opposition.

Cardiff City, like Bolton, don't look out of place in the Championship upon their return to the division, as Brian Barry-Murphy has got the Bluebirds playing some scintillating stuff, and in truth, football that is akin to one of the very best in the league.

Unfortunately for Cardiff, despite the sheer number of chances they are able to produce, they have lacked a consistent clinical touch, and though most supporters would be happy with survival, few can't help but feel it could be something more.

AI thinks they will be a Championship club again, but they won't build much beyond that.

AI says: Continue their remarkable rise but find life increasingly difficult against bigger, better-funded clubs.

Wrexham have had a difficult start to the year under Phil Parkinson, for a change, as the Welsh outfit, for the first time since the National League, must seriously consider a change in leadership sooner rather than later if results don't drastically improve.

Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney have invested heavily in the club, both on and off the pitch, and will be expecting a return on that investment before too long, as AI believes they will be a Championship club once again next year.

Beyond that, the Red Dragons, by AI's account, will suffer a bit of a drop and be much closer to the bottom three than the top eight.

AI says: Have enough quality to survive, although their promotion momentum eventually fades.

The second promoted club on this list, AI believes Huddersfield Town, under Martin Drury, will have what it takes to fire themselves to glory this season, with the likes of Joe Taylor, Derensili Sanches Fernandes, and Archie Collins leading the way.

The Terriers are backed to carry that momentum into next campaign and survive comfortably, which, if you ask any Huddersfield supporter for that outcome right now, they'd surely bite your hand off.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top nine toughest fanbases in the EFL Championship right now from least to most

AI says: A respectable first season back, with some impressive results but occasional defensive problems.

The final promoted club, and their first time playing in the second tier since 2002, as well as their first time since it was rebranded to the Championship, Stockport County are backed to continue their rise through the EFL by securing promotion this season.

With Jimmy McNulty replacing Dave Challinor at the helm at Edgeley Park, the Hatters have been backed by AI to not only secure promotion in 2027, but to comfortably survive in 2028, in what would be an incredible achievement for the club.

AI says: Improve on their current struggles but remain an unpredictable and inconsistent side.

Watford have been tipped by many to face the drop this year, with numerous obvious issues both on and off the pitch at Vicarage Road.

Italian owner Gino Pozzo recently appeared in a Spanish court after being accused of committing tax offences relating to Granada, as meanwhile, Watford hover just above the relegation zone, with a mismanaged summer window compounding a difficult year thus far.

Whether Alessio Dionisi makes it to the end of the season remains to be seen, but you'd do well to find any Hornets fan who wouldn't be happy with AI's prediction to not only stay in the Championship this year, but next year as well.

AI says: Their usual competitiveness and physicality keep them safe, although they lack the quality for a promotion push.

Millwall, off the back of a 3rd place finish in the Championship last season, have struggled to hit those heights again this time around under Alex Neil, as the Scottish boss will point to the sheer amount of injuries they have suffered to key personnel.

AI believes the Lions won't have enough to turn their campaign around and fire themselves towards promotion, maintaining their place in the second tier, before slipping down the division towards the mid-table mediocrity zone.

#2037. Mikkel Ladefoged is Lorent Tolaj 2.0 for Lincoln City

Lincoln City star-power recruit Mikkel Ladefoged has the potential to be the difference maker for the Imps this season, and has a blueprint to copy.

The side jointly-managed by Tom Shaw and Chris Cohen might have lost their most recent three games, but have four wins in the Championship next to their name, including an impressive 4-1 victory over Burnley.

Lincoln sit five points above the drop zone after almost a third of the season. That is a good start for a team promoted last term, heavily tipped to return straight back to League One, and under somewhat new management.

Michael Skubala is under-fire at Bristol City, having jumped ship from the Imps after completing a historic and impressive title win. That left Shaw and Cohen to lead Lincoln, having been elevated from their backroom staff positions.

Lincoln City’s return to the Championship has been 65 years in the making, and they have prepared for it in a risky way.

And, they have done that admirably to date. Avoiding relegation has to be the aim for the Lincolnshire outfit, and they have started well enough to sit outside of the dreaded drop zone. A key part of that early success has been the strikers who made the difference last season.

Ben House (against Bolton Wanderers) and Freddie Draper (against both Preston North End and Bristol City) scored the only goals of 1-0 wins. But, there is a more headline-grabbing attacker who has begun to make a difference too.

Signed by the Imps in the summer for a club record fee, Ladefoged left Swedish outfit Vasteras SK after netting 19 goals in 29 games for his previous club. The fee is believed to be beyond that of the £2.5million paid for commanding Romanian international centre-back Andrei Coubis.

With the hefty price tag, relative to the club’s previous deals, Ladefoged came with high hopes and a large weight rested on his shoulders for the relegation fight. He has shown enough already to prove himself as the key to potential Lincoln success.

The 6’8” Dane took a while to get his first league start, but marked it with a brace against Burnley. He followed that up with an assist in defeat to Birmingham City, and has looked a real threat at the top end of the pitch.

Mikkel Ladefoged career stats by club (credit: Fotmob)

Across nine appearances, he has three goals, netting a late equaliser against Southampton off the bench in the weeks after his signing. The 23-year-old’s height, physicality, pace, and decision-making make him the perfect striker for Lincoln and their quest for continued Championship status.

He has the potential to score plenty more as well, having shown his willingness to create chances for his teammates as well as scoring his own.

In 2010-11 Adel Taarabt ran Championship defences ragged as QPR won the title. Now it’s your turn: weave him past cones, lunging defenders and flying slide tackles, and get the ball in the net at the end of each level. There are 15 levels and only three lives. How far can you take him?

A Football League World arcade game. Best played with sound on.

He fits the mould of Lorent Tolaj. The 25-year-old Swiss striker has found goals hard to come by since being elevated to the Championship this summer. He signed for Skubala’s Bristol City after a spell-binding campaign at Plymouth Argyle.

In League One, Tolaj found the net 18 times across 33 games, being only three others in the top scorer charts. Considering he missed a portion of the latter stages of the season due to injury, it is an impressive return.

It has been a fast rise for Tolaj, scoring 25 in a season in the National League, then recording 24 goal involvements the following term in League Two before his move to Plymouth.

He does not match Ladefoged for height, as very few do, but his pace and power are a real comparison. Tolaj finds space in tight pockets in and around the box, shifts through seemingly too narrow alleys to create dangerous shooting opportunities.

Ladefoged is a similar archetype, and could propel well beyond Tolaj given his additional qualities and early signs in a Lincoln shirt.

Simply put, if the Imps can keep Ladefoged firing and craft a unit that suits his strengths, then relegation will be very little of a concern come the end of the Championship campaign.

#2034. Barry Bannan to change career? Sheffield Wednesday star’s exploits have caused a reaction

Sheffield Wednesday are rebuilding themselves as a club and institution on the pitch this season but their rebuild goes deeper and further than that off it, needing to reconnect with supporters and get back in touch with their history.

Having gone into administration last season, Sheffield Wednesday eventually succumbed to an inevitable relegation, albeit a defeat of West Bromwich Albion on the final day of the season at Hillsborough did help them finish the season on zero points rather than in the minuses.

The Owls have since started this season in a mixed manner, leading to the departure of manager Henrik Pedersen and the subsequent appointment of Dave Challinor.

Such was the mess the club had got into, on-pitch improvement would naturally always have to be subject to so-called ‘teething issues’, while the off-the-pitch commercial aspect of the club also needed improvement.

As a part of that potential rebuild off the pitch and increased commercialisation of the club as it seeks to reconnect with supporters, Wednesday have launched a collaboration with esteemed artist Pete McKee.

60-year-old McKee, born in Sheffield and a cartoonist for the Sheffield Telegraph, has built his artistic reputation on depicting working class elements of society and specifically northern culture – and even more specifically, Sheffield culture.

Within this new collaboration, it has been launched at Riverside Fish and Chip shop on Langsett Road in Hillsborough, nearby to the famous Hillsborough Tap pub and just around the corner from the home ground of Sheffield Wednesday.

FLW’s Sheffield Wednesday fan pundit has reacted to yet another crushing injury blow to defender Max Lowe.

As a part of the launch, club legend, or at the very least cult hero, Barry Bannan has featured in the photoshoot dressed as a chippy worker behind the counter.

The actual collaboration centres on the launch of a range of clothing such as hoodies and t-shirts with McKee’s Wednesday-focused art as the design.

McKee has explained: “I’ve supported Wednesday ever since I was a nipper, with my two elder brothers taking it in turns to take me until I was old enough to go by myself with my mates.

“The club has been a part of my DNA throughout my life and career, so it’s with immense pride that I now have the opportunity to work directly with the club on this range.

“I hope the fans take it to their hearts, as well all share the same love of following the Wednesday.”

Naturally, there has been quite the response from Sheffield Wednesday supporters to the comically produced involvement of Bannan in the photoshoot.

Many have expressed their amusement with the 36-year-old, soon to be 37, getting involved to such a degree with The Owls’ social media post nudging him to ensure he doesn’t give up his ‘day job’.

However, given the mixed performances of Bannan on the pitch, one Wednesday supporter did quip that perhaps the Scotsman may be best suited to the role he has been pictured in.

Having spent nine and a half years at Hillsborough, making over 475 appearances for the club in his first stint in South Yorkshire, Bannan moved to Millwall in January.

More of a bit-part player for The Lions as they finished third in the Championship before losing to eventual play-off winners Hull City in the play-off semi-final, Bannan returned from the capital city with Wednesday set to relaunch themselves as an entity this summer and this season.

18 new signings came through the door, including Bannan, and there were some standout performances and moments in the early couple of months, such as a 7-2 victory over Bromley and a 5-0 shellacking of AFC Wimbledon.

Inconsistency in terms of performances and results getting worse on the pitch, especially away from home, led to the departure of Henrik Pedersen with former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor now tasked with ensuring a title challenge in League One.

That inconsistency and general level of frustration felt by supporters has perhaps best been represented by the dip of Bannan’s own level; not quite as protective of possession nor as dynamic with or without the ball as he was in the past.

The arrival of Challinor could and perhaps should spark a Wednesday surge – and there will have to be improvement from their still talismanic figure in the middle of the park to help that along.

#2033. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2031. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

In the summer, Palladino turned down a long-term contract with Atalanta because he was linked with more prestigious jobs, but this left him without a job. Then, when Bologna parted ways with Domenico Tedesco, the Italian took his talents to Reggio Emilia and has not looked back.

Why didn’t he stay in Bergamo? The question arises naturally, considering the results obtained and qualification for the Conference despite a stuttering start. Palladino – after the victory against Borussia Dortmund – was considered the future for La Dea.

There was a contract ready to continue together until 2029, but everything seemed to turn sour. The three-year contract that was then offered to Maurizio Sarri, because Atalanta needed a decision quickly and Palladino wanted time to reflect.

His contract with Atalanta expired in 2027, and he wasn’t in a hurry to sign another. The second thoughts didn’t sit well with Atalanta but Palladino later backtracked, offering to accept the previous contract, even offering to shorten it to 2028.

Meanwhile, Atalanta’s league performance worsened and they failed to reach the Coppa Italia final, against Sarri himself. Relations, now strained, finally broke down.

The truth is that the former Monza coach was waiting to see which vacancies came up. Napoli in particular were a club he was monitoring closely, when Antonio Conte announced his departure. Palladino, along with Vincenzo Italiano, was a strong name.

There could also have been an opportunity at Milan when Massimiliano Allegri departed. However, as is known, the Rossoneri decided to pursue Andoni Iraola and then turned to Ruben Amorim, clearly not inclined to bet on a coach who knows the league. Palladino would have been keen, it seems.

#2029. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

#2028. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2027. 3 in, 3 out: How Birmingham City's dream January transfer window looks

Birmingham City are flying high in the Championship at present, with Chris Davies' side leading the division across the November international break.

Blues are ahead of Middlesbrough and Stoke City as a result of their superior goal difference after 15 matches, with it now remaining to be seen if they can match or better such performance levels.

Such feats come after an interesting summer of activity, during which fewer additions and sales were made at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park than in years gone by, whilst newly-appointed director of football, John Murtough, is set to oversee his first recruitment drive.

With that said, Football League World have looked at what an ideal January window could look like for Birmingham amid their promotion hopes.

Getting things underway would be an attempted pursuit for FC Lorient's Arthur Avom, with FLW exclusively revealing Birmingham's interest in the 21-year-old alongside that of Middlesbrough.

Despite being relatively young, Avom's impressive performances for the French side have attracted the attention of several Premier League sides, as well as other top-flight sides across Europe, with valuations as high as £17.8m touted in the meantime.

He hasn't let such speculation impact his early-season performances for Lorient either, and with his contract expiring next June, Birmingham could eye a potential cut-price deal for his services, should Avom's current employers not seek to tie him down to fresh terms in the coming weeks.

Another cut-price deal which may arise for Davies and his recruitment team is one for Canadian international, Liam Millar, who has certainly made his mark already at St. Andrew's on loan from Hull City.

Blues fended off interest from the two sides directly below them in the table to land the winger's services for the season, and after netting for the Tigers in the Premier League against Coventry, Millar has since produced four goals and three assists in his 11 Championship appearances so far this term.

Those in East Yorkshire have also been left confused by the 27-year-old's recent admissions in interviews, and whilst Hull have the option to extend his contract until June 2028, it could make sense for all parties to wrap up a permanent deal as early as January.

Birmingham's two main attackers, August Priske and Jay Stansfield, have caused plenty of havoc for defences so far this season, but there are question marks beyond the duo.

Having been linked with a return last January, as well as being the subject of interest from local rivals, Wolves, in the summer, Birmingham could explore a reunion with Scotland international, Che Adams, seven years after his departure for Southampton.

However, how feasible this deal would be remains to be seen, as the experienced striker is now in his third season with Torino, and has already scored four goals in his first nine Serie A outings this season under Ignazio Abate.

Middlesbrough's Kim Hellberg and Swansea City's Vitor Matos are on the radar of Crystal Palace, which could be good news for their promotion rivals.

Lee Buchanan has become rather forgotten about at St. Andrew's, with the last two years being a tale of injury misfortune for the Birmingham defender.

The 25-year-old hasn't featured competitively for 23 months, with a serious knee injury followed by further setbacks, and he is now firmly behind Alex Cochrane and Kristoffer Lund in the pecking order.

Buchanan attracted interest from Luton Town and Reading in the summer, and it would be no surprise to see transfer links surround him in January, with it appearing that an exit could be the best decision for his long-term career.

Marvin Ducksch's immediate future at St. Andrew's has been up in the air for some time, and it wouldn't be the greatest of surprises to see last summer's £1.75m arrival find a new club this winter.

Ducksch hit double-figures last season, but after being charged for causing a three-vehicle collision in April, the two-time German international has been the subject of heavy exit talk.

Blues fans, will Marvin Ducksch stay or go this January? Comment below!

Indeed, it was suggested that the forward came mightily close to joining Valencia on Deadline Day before a deal between the two clubs collapsed, and since then, he has started in none of his nine Championship appearances so far this season.

Scott Wright was recently inserted back into Birmingham's 25-man squad following Kanya Fujimoto's loan move to Tokyo Verdy, but a swift departure for the 29-year-old winger also seems inevitable.

After featuring heavily in all competitions two seasons ago after signing from Rangers, Wright suffered a serious injury against Reading last February, and only made a full recovery in the latter weeks of 2025.

Since then, an underwhelming loan with Dundee FC and limited minutes with Blues have followed, meaning that if the Scottish youth international wants to source regular minutes, it would be elsewhere rather than being behind Carlos Vicente and Patrick Roberts in Davies' pecking order.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2026. Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

That was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he said, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

In terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

“We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

“We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”

"We need to help them, not to rely everything on them" Xabi Alonso speaking about Chelsea's 'special' front three 🔵 pic.twitter.com/JnSBoNexF4

"Arsenal DON'T win the league if they have Ramsdale and not Raya" 🧤@Carra23 and @GNev2 think that upgrading the goalkeeper position could be the 'last piece' for Chelsea 🧩 pic.twitter.com/UBzMCFmxpp

"You can see in his eyes, he's ready to prove people wrong""Best player on the pitch by a mile" 👏Morgan Rogers reacts to his debut and the performance of Cole Palmer pic.twitter.com/M7JKk1MQ8U

"How ready are you?""Did you not watch the game?" 😅Cole Palmer says he is 'hungry' and ready to get back to his best! pic.twitter.com/xpg5zJl9k0

2 - Cole Palmer tonight vs Fulham:1 goal1 assist5 dribbles completed5 shots3 chances created7 ball recoveries10 duels wonHe was only the second player on record since 2006-07 to record all of these numbers in a Premier League game.Cold. pic.twitter.com/uW4YPeHNnD

“There were things to really like. On paper, that front three [for Chelsea] is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. [Morgan] Rogers’ first game, what a start. But when you think of him, [Cole] Palmer and Pedro; that is as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

“But I do think concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it is going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight.”

“The attacking play, Cole Palmer was sensational. If you talk about Cole Palmer getting back to his best you have got a £120m-£125m player there. [Morgan] Rogers getting a goal. Those two being electric with Joao Pedro up front. The front three were brilliant tonight. One of the best things I have seen this weekend.

“They have added an experience player at centre-back, centre midfield and centre forward. I do not know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement [Robert] Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It is a problem.”
